title: OmniEgoCap: Device-Agnostic Sequence-Level Egocentric Motion Reconstruction
claim: Our method reconstructs coherent, long-sequence full-body motion in large scenes from very different egocentric cameras.
layout: 2 panels, top frame strips above 3D scene reconstructions, dotted trajectory arrows
description: A wide two-panel figure. The top row of each panel is a strip of egocentric video frames with timestamps (0:06 to 6:03). The left strip is from a GoPro and shows color first-person views of kitchen tasks, with a blurred wearer portrait at the far left. The right strip is from an Aria and shows grayscale fisheye frames of a large indoor space, with a blurred portrait at the far right. Below each strip is a 3D scene point cloud with many overlaid SMPL body meshes. The left meshes are pink and the right meshes are blue. Dotted black arrows trace the wearer's path through time. The eye goes first to the dense, colorful body meshes and the long trajectories. Together they show consistent motion over minutes across two devices.
caption: OmniEgoCap is a sequence-level diffusion framework that combines long-range body and camera-observation invariants with geometry-aware visibility augmentation to reconstruct consistent 3D full-body motion across diverse egocentric devices. (L) GoPro and (R) Aria.
abstract: Commercial egocentric devices capture human behavior in everyday settings, yet full-body motion reconstruction must generalize across diverse cameras and mountings. This is challenging because head trajectories under-determine body motion, while hand observations are intermittent and camera-dependent: a hand may disappear simply because it has left the camera's field of view. Existing methods treat such absences as missing data, relying on fixed visibility regimes or post-hoc optimization, and fail to generalize across devices. We present OmniEgoCap, a sequence-level diffusion framework for device-agnostic egocentric full-body motion reconstruction. Our key insight is that egocentric videos contain sequence-level evidence about both the wearer and the camera-induced visibility structure, enabling OmniEgoCap to infer consistent body shape and coherent motion from sparse head and hand cues. To prevent overfitting to a single camera setup, we further introduce geometry-aware visibility augmentation, which synthesizes visibility patterns from realistic variations in camera geometry. We also present OmniEgoDB, the first mocap benchmark that pairs ground-truth motion with recordings from multiple consumer egocentric devices. Experiments on synthetic, real-device, and in-the-wild settings demonstrate superior motion reconstruction, robust cross-device generalization, and coherent in-the-wild results.
